category_title: High school students with learning disabilities and ADHD who struggle to break down multi-step algebraic tasks
scenario_title: Conceptual error when multiplying binomials abstractly
minimal_context: Marcia is multiplying the binomials (x + 3) and (x + 5) using only abstract notation during a one-on-one instructional session.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's try multiplying (x + 3) and (x + 5) using only the abstract symbolism on your paper.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: It’s so much more hard because it’s not broken up then. Like what I do is I see the blocks and I read it and I write it then I move it.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Just try to do it with the numbers this time.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: But when it’s all numbers then I forgot where to break it up and what’s what.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Write down what you think the answer is.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Okay, I'll just multiply the x's and the numbers. It's x2 + 15. Is that right? I can't tell if it's right without the blocks.
